title: Omdia: foldable OLED panel shipments to jump 44% in 2026
content: Omdia says that following the latest wide-format foldable smartphone launches by both Apple and Samsung, foldable OLED panel shipments will reach 29 million units in 2026, up 44% from 2025.

title: Apple's iPhone Duo sees high demand, preorders sell out within minutes and deliveries slip to late January
content: Apple started taking preorders for its first foldable smartphone, the iPhone Duo, on October 16 - and demand seems to be very strong. The initial stock sold out within minutes in the US, Korea, Germany and other markets, and within half an hour the delivery dates for new orders slipped from November to December, and then to late January 2027. title: SK Materials JNC and SN Display to establish a mass production system for perovskite nanocrystal emitters
content: Korea's SK Materials JNC (SKMJ) announced that it has signed an MoU with SN Display to establish a mass production system for SN Display's perovskite materials. The two companies aim to take perovskite emitters from the research stage to a level that can be used by the display industry.

title: Micron reaches deal with Taiwan union to introduce quarterly profit bonuses in FY27
content: Micron Technology's labor dispute in Taiwan appears set for resolution after its Taichung union signed a labor-management agreement with the company and withdrew from the mediation session scheduled for October 22. According to an internal email circulated by employees, Micron will introduce quarterly profit-sharing bonuses based on employee level in fiscal year 2027. The plan will cover employees at the director level and below.

title: Cloud AI to drive chip growth in 2027 as Taiwan suppliers seek opportunities beyond weak consumer edge AI
content: Market expectations for cloud AI demand have generally remained bullish through 2028-2029, with order visibility extending clearly over the next two to three years. The outlook for 2027 is therefore similarly positive.

title: Sony keeps chip unit as imaging sensors, TSMC partnership drive strategy
content: Sony Group will not spin off its semiconductor business, which focuses on image sensors, president and CEO Hiroki Totoki said recently. The group is retaining the unit because its imaging-sensor expertise creates synergies between components and creative production, while a partnership with Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC) will support future manufacturing investment.

title: Samsung shifts M2800 modem to 2nm, frees 4nm capacity for HBM base dies
content: Samsung Electronics is transitioning its 4nm production capacity to HBM, with its next-generation mobile modem, the M2800, set to move to a 2nm process. The freed 4nm capacity will primarily support production of HBM base dies, which handle control functions at the bottom of HBM stacks.

title: Samsung Display accelerates MPO and inkjet OLED development for laptops and monitors
content: Samsung Display (SDC) is reportedly advancing both micro-patterned OLED (MPO) and inkjet-printed OLED technologies in parallel, expanding its non-fine metal mask (non-FMM) RGB OLED lineup. SDC is currently validating high-resolution fabrication processes using a 7-inch engineering sample for MPO, while evaluating a pilot line for inkjet printing, with initial commercial targets focused on IT panels such as notebooks and desktop monitors.

title: Anthropic's IPO spotlight falls on its potential US$750 billion AI compute tab
content: Anthropic's draft IPO prospectus captures the tension behind its rapid growth: first-half revenue surged to US$16.3 billion, while the company reported a US$80.7 billion net loss and outlined potential computing commitments of up to US$750 billion.
